extracted.intended_audience: NLP and narrative-studies researchers working on LLM-based story generation, annotation, and evaluation
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines and evaluative criteria for using large language models (and smaller/fine-tuned models) to generate, annotate, and evaluate narrative texts, and for designing datasets/metrics for narrative NLP tasks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of prompting for story generation vs fine-tuning for understanding tasks
rubrics_metrics.description: Survey finding: "story generation tasks exclusively use prompt-engineering techniques while fine-tuning is reserved for understanding tasks."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For generation, prefer prompt-based (zero/few-shot) methods; fine-tuning is more commonly applied to classification/understanding tasks. There is no established supervised or reinforcement learning method for story generation in the reviewed literature.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prefer simpler prompting strategies for efficiency
rubrics_metrics.description: "There is a trend of simpler prompting strategies prevailing over complex ones due to similar performance and better efficiency."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Default to simpler prompt designs unless more complex prompts demonstrably improve performance; report comparative efficiency and accuracy when choosing complex prompts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Zero-shot prompting as a cost-effective, often sufficient approach
rubrics_metrics.description: "Zero-shot prompting is often chosen ... A significant reason is cost consideration ... zero-shot prompting is sufficient at achieving near-optimal performance."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider zero-shot prompting first for cost/resource limited settings and benchmark against few-shot and fine-tuned baselines; justify choice with empirical comparisons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Role-prompting / structured zero-shot classification framework
rubrics_metrics.description: Piper and Bagga's zero-shot prompting framework consists of: "role prompt, framing question, ordinal scale, narrative feature, and individual passage to quantitatively classify the degree of presence of narrative discourse features."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When building zero-shot classifiers for narrative features, include explicit role/system prompt, a framing question, a clear ordinal scale for labels, the targeted narrative feature definition, and the passage to be evaluated; provide examples and output format for replicability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mixture-of-Personas (MoP) prompting to capture diverse judgements
rubrics_metrics.description: MoP builds personas (e.g., empathy-specialist, narrative-complexity assessor) and averages their judgements to reflect multifaceted human assessment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design multiple domain-expert personas focusing on different components (e.g., Psychological Depth Scale facets), prompt each persona separately, and aggregate (average) outputs to approximate a diversity of human opinions; report persona definitions and aggregation method.

rubrics_metrics.name: Chain-of-thought and iterative prompting for generation and evaluative reasoning
rubrics_metrics.description: Chain-of-thought prompting and iterative prompting strategies are used to expand generation and to answer yes/no criteria assessing creative writing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use chain-of-thought or plan-and-write prompts when reasoning/stepwise evaluation is needed; iterative prompting can be used to expand story length or refine outputs. Note: some studies found LLM assessments using chain-of-thought did not correlate with expert assessments—validate against human judgements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specify inference hyperparameters for replicability
rubrics_metrics.description: Studies specify parameters such as temperature, top-p, and frequency penalty (examples: temperature = 0.7, top_p = 0.5; elsewhere temperature = 0.9 and frequency_penalty = 0.2). Chun justified lower-limit choices: "lower temperature values of less than 0.5 did not produce distributions with informative statistical spread."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Always report inference settings (temperature, top-p, frequency_penalty, response format). If choosing non-default values, justify and, where useful, explore sensitivity to these settings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stabilise outputs via prompt paraphrases and majority voting
rubrics_metrics.description: Use multiple paraphrases of the original question (e.g., five paraphrases) and take a per-text majority vote among independent outputs as the final label.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When LLM outputs are sensitive to wording, generate outputs from multiple paraphrases and aggregate (majority vote or other ensemble) to reduce label variance; report paraphrase generation method and aggregation rule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Replica human annotation instructions in LLM prompts
rubrics_metrics.description: Researchers sometimes use the same instructions given to human annotators (e.g., Mechanical Turk guidelines) as LLM prompts, or prompt LLMs with a detailed codebook replicating human annotation instructions to rate features such as vividness and plot volume.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To improve comparability, translate human annotation guidelines/codebooks verbatim into LLM prompts; document the prompt and any adaptations, and compare LLM outputs to human annotations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Validate LLM annotations against human annotations with correlation/agreement metrics
rubrics_metrics.description: Validity tested by comparisons using metrics such as Spearman correlation, Pearson correlation, Kendall's Tau, and inter-annotator agreement measures (e.g., Fleiss' scores).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate LLM-generated annotations by computing appropriate correlation/coherence/agreement statistics against human labels; report which metric was used and why, and include confidence/bootstrapping where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Measure discrete narrative features rather than holistic aesthetic value
rubrics_metrics.description: The survey emphasizes the lack of agreed standards for "quality or aesthetic value" and recommends focusing on measurable aspects: coherence, causality, role dynamics, vividness, plot volume, narrativity, etc. Frameworks like HEART and Piper & Bagga's fifteen measurable features operationalise such components.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Define and operationalise individual narrative features to be measured (with codebooks/annotations). Prefer narrowly scoped metrics for a single aspect rather than attempting a single overall narrative-quality score.

rubrics_metrics.name: Develop specific single-aspect metrics instead of all-encompassing benchmarks
rubrics_metrics.description: "Instead of ambitiously aiming for an all-encompassing benchmark that measures a narrative as a whole, focus on developing metrics that measure only a single aspect of narrative."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design and validate focused metrics (e.g., coherence-only, causality-only, surprise-only). Show construct validity and reliability for each metric before combining them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Justify and report model & fine-tuning choices and hyperparameters
rubrics_metrics.description: Model selection and tuning choices (e.g., Phi3-7B chosen because base model had highest performance; LoRA rank=64 alpha=16; learning rates like 2e-5 or 3e-4; epochs 2–3; batch sizes and GPU types) materially affect outcomes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When fine-tuning or distilling, report model name/size, optimizer, learning rate, LoRA or adapter settings, number of epochs, batch size, hardware, and dataset composition/size/quality. Justify model choice with baseline performance if possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fine-tune on smaller, higher-quality validation sets to improve accuracy
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors found that tuning the model on a smaller but higher quality validation set further improved accuracy (example: improved to 0.80 on the test set).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider curated high-quality validation sets for early stopping/hyperparameter search rather than large noisy splits; report validation selection criteria and resulting performance changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consider encoder models and probability outputs for classification tasks
rubrics_metrics.description: Sui et al. used a fine-tuned encoder ELECTRA-large model using the softmax probability output and outperforms zero-shot and few-shot decoder-based models like GPT-4 on story detection classification tasks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not assume decoder-only models are always best for narrative classification; evaluate encoder architectures and use calibrated probability outputs where helpful; report calibration and thresholds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distillation practice: mask instructions, train on completions for gains
rubrics_metrics.description: Piper and Bagga found major performance gains when masking out the instructions and training on only completions in model distillation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When distilling from a large teacher, experiment with training on teacher completions without instruction text; document masking strategy and compare with instruction-inclusive distillation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid unnecessary pre-processing that can harm zero-shot/topic labeling
rubrics_metrics.description: Pre-processing of passages, such as summarisation, resulted in poorer model responses in a zero-shot topic labeling study.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Test whether intermediate preprocessing steps (summaries, chunking, etc.) improve or harm performance—do not assume preprocessing is beneficial; report ablation results.

rubrics_metrics.name: LLMs are sensitive to small prompt changes and low-bit quantisation
rubrics_metrics.description: Small changes in prompt wording can affect model performance; lower-bit quantisation decreased performance; including special characters as markers did not significantly increase performance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Perform robustness checks for prompt wording and quantisation; if using markers or special tokens, report experiments showing benefit (or lack thereof).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use random-string injection to avoid server-side caching when testing parametric memory
rubrics_metrics.description: Chun injected unique random strings to avoid possible server-side caching when relying on model parametric memory to surface texts seen during pre-training.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When probing parametric memory or collecting outputs that might be cached, include nonce tokens/random strings in prompts to mitigate caching artifacts and report nonce usage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Iterative prompting for length control: expand outputs to target length
rubrics_metrics.description: Chakrabarty et al. use iterative prompting to expand generated story until the output length reaches the desired amount, because LLMs tend to produce outputs 20–50% more concise than intended.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For length-sensitive generation, implement iterative expansion or controlled decoding techniques, and report pre/post lengths and the number of iterations required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Continued pre-training on domain/language-specific corpora for low-resource gains
rubrics_metrics.description: Continued pre-training on domain and language-specific corpora further enhances performance in low-resource settings (e.g., Irish and Scottish Gaelic folk-tales).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To improve performance for niche domains/languages, perform domain-adaptive pre-training on curated corpora and report corpus composition and impact on downstream tasks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Need for standardised benchmarks for coherence, causality, and role dynamics
rubrics_metrics.description: "Standardised benchmarks for narrative coherence, causality, and role dynamics remain lacking."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritise creation of benchmark tasks/datasets with clear task definitions and annotation guidelines for these specific narrative dimensions; document inter-annotator agreement and evaluation protocols.

rubrics_metrics.name: Account for cultural bias and cross-cultural framing in narrative evaluation
rubrics_metrics.description: Cross-cultural studies show name cues trigger stereotypes and that models can subvert and reinforce cultural norms; narrative perception varies by reader context.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design datasets and evaluation protocols to test for cultural bias, include diverse name/cultural contexts, report demographic/contextual variables, and measure differential model behaviour across groups.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treat output variability as a potential proxy for annotator diversity, but validate
rubrics_metrics.description: Some studies claim that variability from different prompts can mimic multiple human annotators and represent variations between human annotators (e.g., Troiano and Vossen compared Fleiss' scores).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider using multiple prompts/parameters to sample annotator-like variability, compare LLM-derived variance to human inter-annotator variance, and validate whether the distributional properties align.

rubrics_metrics.name: Beware low correlation between some LLM evaluations and expert judgements; share evaluation methods
rubrics_metrics.description: Several studies report low to moderate correlation between LLM outputs and human annotations and some LLM assessment methods did not correlate positively with expert assessments; lack of shared evaluation methods hinders comparison.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When proposing automatic evaluation methods, compare against expert human judgements, report correlation statistics, and publish evaluation prompts/codebooks to facilitate cross-study comparisons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dataset and annotation recommendations: multilingual, human-annotated, long-form coverage
rubrics_metrics.description: Gaps include multilingual corpora, human-annotated datasets, and labelled long-form narratives. Existing corpora are often English-only and theory work centres on Western traditions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritise creating multilingual, human-annotated, and long-form narrative datasets; document annotation guidelines, cultural provenance, and licensing to increase reusability and fairness.
